fr.elements: Main Residence; Detached Structure; Front Driveway; Access Drive; Vehicle Parking Area; Open Terrain; Landscaped Area; Perimeter Fencing
fr.considerations: Single Access Point; Long Driveway; Dense Vegetation; Limited Turnaround Space; Open Terrain
fr.recommendations:
• Install a reflective address marker at the driveway entrance visible from both directions on the road.
• Mark the single driveway entrance clearly so responders can identify it quickly at night or in reduced visibility.
• Clear vegetation along both sides of the access drive to maintain an unobstructed travel path for emergency vehicles.
• Trim tree branches overhanging the access drive to allow full-size emergency vehicles to pass without obstruction.
• Designate and mark a turnaround area near the main residence large enough for a fire apparatus or ambulance to reverse direction.
• Keep the turnaround area free of parked vehicles, equipment, and stored materials at all times.
• Install a sign or marker at the detached structure to help responders distinguish it from the main residence on arrival.
• Keep the parking area clear of vehicles that could block responder staging space near the residence.
• If perimeter fencing includes a gate across the access drive, keep that gate unlocked or install a Knox Box or responder-compatible lock to allow immediate entry.
• Post the property address on or near any driveway gate so responders can confirm the correct property before entry.
• Thin dense vegetation alongside the access drive so responders on foot can move between the drive and the open terrain without obstruction.

wildfire.conditions: Scattered Shrubs; Tree Cluster; Vegetation Near Structure; Scattered Trees; Open Terrain; Brush Area; Grass Cover; Limited Vegetation Separation; Multiple Access Routes; Vegetation Along Driveway; Scattered Shrubs; Open Green Space
wildfire.recommendations:
• Trim shrubs that are growing directly next to the structure to create open space between the plants and the building.
• Thin the tree cluster to increase spacing between individual trees and reduce how easily fire can move from one tree to the next.
• Remove or cut back shrubs and brush growing along the driveway to keep it clear for vehicles to pass through safely.
• Trim any overhanging tree branches that extend over the driveway or roofline.
• Cut grass near the structure short and keep it mowed regularly, especially during dry periods.
• Clear dead grass, leaves, and loose plant material that has collected against or near the structure.
• Thin scattered trees near the structure so there is open ground between their canopies and the building.
• Remove brush from areas where it connects directly to trees or shrubs near the structure, breaking up the continuous path of vegetation.
• Keep the area immediately surrounding the structure free of shrub regrowth by checking and cutting it back regularly.
• Clear brush and tall grass from the edges of all driveways and access routes to maintain open lanes for emergency vehicles.
• Thin shrubs in the brush area nearest the structure so individual plants are separated by open ground rather than growing together in a dense mass.
